items.question: By what mantra should one worship Shankara?
premises: Worship of Shankara is being considered
A mantra is sought as the means of worship
items.inference: The appropriate mantra for worshipping Shankara must be identified
items.plain_english: By what mantra, O Shankara, should I worship you?

items.question: Which mantra is to be employed in that worship?
premises: A mantra is required for worship
The specific mantra to be used is not yet stated
items.inference: The speaker asks to be told which mantra should be employed
items.plain_english: And tell me, which mantra is to be employed there?

items.question: What mantra is used to worship Shankara in this teaching?
premises: The question of the mantra for worship continues
Shankara is addressed directly
items.inference: The speaker seeks the mantra for worshipping Shankara
items.plain_english: With this mantra, O Shankara, I worship you.

items.question: Can the mantra called silence serve to worship the Lord?
premises: A mantra named silence is identified
The Lord is worshipped through this mantra
items.inference: Silence itself functions as the mantra for worshipping the Lord
items.plain_english: I worship the Lord with the mantra called silence.

items.question: How can mere exhalation become the practice of steadfastness?
premises: Steadfastness is practiced
The means is nothing more than exhalation
items.inference: Simple exhalation suffices as the practice of steadfastness
items.plain_english: By mere exhalation, I practice steadfastness.

items.question: What remains to be done for you when all already belongs to you?
premises: Everything already belongs to the addressee
The need for further action is questioned
items.inference: No additional offering or action is necessary
items.plain_english: All is yours; what is there to be done for you?

items.question: What can be obtained for the sake of worshipping you?
premises: Worship of the addressee is intended
The speaker finds nothing to obtain for that purpose
items.inference: Nothing external can be acquired as a means for worship
items.plain_english: For the sake of your worship, I obtain nothing at all.

items.question: How does breath become the means by which all is known?
premises: All is to be known
Breath is identified as the means
items.inference: Breath serves as the medium through which all is known
items.plain_english: By that breath, all is to be known.

items.question: What does abandoning the entire mass of entities as ash accomplish?
premises: The whole mass of entities is abandoned
It is treated as mere ash
items.inference: Renouncing all entities as insubstantial leads beyond attachment
items.plain_english: Having abandoned the entire mass of entities as if it were ash.

items.question: What is given when self is offered to you and to me?
premises: Something is given to the self
The giving involves both you and me
items.inference: The self is recognized as given in relation to both self and other
uncertainties: exact syntactic relation of cya+ta in this vernacular form
items.plain_english: To me and to you, it is given to the self.

items.question: How does knowing you lead to attaining repose today?
premises: Knowledge has arisen
Repose is attained in relation to you
items.inference: Knowing you brings the speaker to repose
items.plain_english: Having known you today, I have come to repose in you.

items.question: Why is innate practice always worthy of being spoken?
premises: Practice is innate
It is always to be affirmed or spoken
items.inference: Innate practice is continuously valid and expressible
items.plain_english: Innate practice is always to be spoken of.

items.question: How does remembrance worship the pure self?
premises: Worship occurs through remembrance
The self is pure
items.inference: Remembrance itself constitutes worship of the pure self
items.plain_english: By remembrance, through which the pure self is worshipped.

items.question: How does recognition reveal what is already near?
premises: What is sought is near
Recognition makes it known
items.inference: Recognition discloses the nearness of what already is
items.plain_english: It is near, and known by recognition.

items.question: What is accomplished by searching in another place?
premises: Searching is directed to another place
The action is already completed or futile
items.inference: Searching elsewhere is unnecessary or already done in vain
items.plain_english: What is done by searching in another place?

items.question: What happens when knowing and not-knowing both fall away there?
premises: Knowing and not-knowing are both invoked
Both come to rest in that place
items.inference: Beyond knowing and not-knowing, one settles in that state
uncertainties: precise nuance of pyana in this context
items.plain_english: To know, not to know, and there indeed to fall.

items.question: To what extent does the mass of embodied beings share the same condition?
premises: Embodied beings are considered as a whole
Their extent or measure is indicated
items.inference: All embodied beings fall within the same measured condition
items.plain_english: Indeed, to whatever extent there is the mass of embodied beings.

items.question: How does contemplative awareness enter within one's own self?
premises: Awareness turns inward
It is established in contemplation of that
items.inference: Contemplative awareness abides within one's own self
items.plain_english: Indeed, entered within one's own self, in contemplation of that.

items.question: What is released when one falls, breaks, and abandons there?
premises: Falling and breaking occur
Abandonment takes place in that state
items.inference: Letting go in that state involves the dissolution of former supports
uncertainties: exact verbal forms and subjects in vernacular
items.plain_english: Fallen, torn, abandoned there.

items.question: How did the speaker become renowned in the world as Lalla?
premises: The speaker is known as Lalla
This renown occurred in the world at that time
items.inference: The speaker attained public recognition under the name Lalla
items.plain_english: Then I became renowned in the world as Lalla.

items.question: How can essence be grasped as having the form of void?
premises: Essence is taken or realized
Its form is described as void
items.inference: The realized essence is apprehended as void in form
items.plain_english: In being, the essence is taken as void in form.

items.question: What is the significance of remembering the void seven times?
premises: The void is remembered
The remembrance occurs seven times
items.inference: Repeated remembrance of the void marks a sustained contemplative act
items.plain_english: Indeed, I remember the void seven times.

items.question: Why is the teaching about Shiva said to be difficult?
premises: The teaching concerns Shiva
The teaching is described as difficult
items.inference: Understanding or attaining Shiva through this teaching is difficult
items.plain_english: Shiva is difficult; such is your teaching.

items.question: Why must Shiva be heard from the guru if attained with difficulty?
premises: Shiva is attainable with difficulty
The teaching is to be heard from the guru
items.inference: Because Shiva is hard to attain, one must receive that teaching from the guru
items.plain_english: Hear: Shiva is attained with difficulty, from the guru.
